title.narrative: Integrated community resilience and empowerment for sustainable development

description.narrative: The Integrated Community Resilience and Empowerment for Sustainable Development project is designed to strengthen the resilience, livelihoods, and rights of poor and marginalized communities in Zambia amid rising socio-economic pressures, climate-related shocks, and a rapidly evolving civic space. Implemented in Chongwe, Chisamba, Lusaka, and Kafue, the project will directly benefit over 11,000 community members and indirectly reach more than 60,000 individuals through expanded value chains, advocacy, and community-led initiatives. Building on lessons from CIVSAM Phase I, the project shifts from a predominantly housing-focused approach to a stronger emphasis on climate-resilient food systems, inclusive markets, and women- and youth-led livelihood opportunities. The project will work closely with established community structures, including the Zambia Homeless and Poor People's Federation, farmer cooperatives, and market leadership structures, ensuring meaningful participation, strengthened ownership, and sustainability. Key interventions include promoting sustainable agriculture, diversified and equitable value chains, communal gardens, and women- and youth-led enterprises. Financial inclusion will be enhanced by strengthening VSLAs and supporting their transition into SACCOs, complemented by digital literacy and increased access to mobile and online financial services. A dedicated Food Systems results area will advance women's land and water rights, secure tenure, and greater participation in local markets. Renewable energy solutions, such as solar drying and organic waste recycling, will reduce food loss, improve incomes, and enhance community resilience. Integrated advocacy, digital platforms like Know Your City TV, and participatory monitoring tools will ensure evidence-based learning and adaptive management. Overall, the project will empower communities to build secure, climate-resilient livelihoods while influencing policies and systems that underpin equitable and sustainable development in Zambia.
